FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=+2SU,MO|20260302T0900.note: A BYDAY list mixing a signed weekdaynum with an unsigned one is a union of its elements, not an intersection. RFC 5545 3.3.10's own example FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=2;COUNT=10;BYDAY=1SU,-1SU expands to the first *and* the last Sunday, and 'BYDAY=MO ... represents all Mondays within the month'; nothing in 3.3.10 makes the elements of the list constrain each other. python-dateutil 2.9.0.post0 splits BYDAY into _byweekday (unsigned) and _bynweekday (signed) and then applies the two as separate exclusion clauses, so a day must match both -- yielding an empty recurrence set when the weekdays differ. Its own BYMONTHDAY handling, three lines below in the same condition, gets the signed/unsigned union right. See finding 013.

FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=1,5;BYWEEKNO=1,52;WK.note: dateutil 2.9.0.post0 misnumbers the days of a year that belong to the previous year's last week; see finding 008. All five disputes disappear under the fix in dateutil/dateutil PR #1537 (open). Expected values are naive's, which agree with week numbering computed from RFC 5545 3.3.10's own definition and, for WKST=MO, with date.isocalendar().

meta.about: Hand adjudications of cases in disputed.json, keyed by '<RRULE>|<DTSTART>'. Applied by build_corpus.py so that regenerating the corpus does not lose them. 'expected' is the value argued for in the cited finding; 'undecided' means the finding concluded that RFC 5545 does not settle the case.
